title: This is how you cast Phantom in 2025!  #ImmersivePhantom #MasqueradeN...
transcript: One aspect of masquerade that I really haven't seen a lot of people talking about is its casting, and specifically its use of colorblind casting. Because people may not realize this, but The Phantom of the opera, during its 30 year run on Broadway, was famously very white. In fact, as far as I can tell, only three POC performers ever played the roles of Phantom or Christine full time on Broadway. Those being Norm Lewis, Emily Kawatchu, and Ali E. Waltz. And so it feels pretty significant to me that when masquerade opens, we have six Phantoms and six christines, six of which are POC performers. Those being Kyle Scatlett, Telly Leung, and Nick Walker for the Phantoms, and Heidi Ferrier, Francesca Marra, and Anna Zavolson for Christine. Like, with one cast, we have now tripled the amount of POC performers that have played these roles full time in New York City. And this kind of diversity is very much present in the entire cast of masquerade. But I want to highlight these two roles specifically because I think it's a really interesting case study. And it does feel like often we get casting announcements that make us feel like we're going backwards in terms of representation. I've certainly done many a video on castings that I think miss the Mark. But I realized I've never made a video praising casting that I think is doing it really well. So I want to make this video just kind of shouting Out the masquerade casting team for assembling a truly phenomenal cast. I think that masquerade pushes the Phantom of the opera story in new directions in so many ways, and I think that is very much reflected in its casting as well.
classificationReason: Discussion of Masquerade (Immersive Phantom)'s colorblind/diverse casting choices for the Phantom and Christine roles — no attendance or first-hand opinion of the production itself.
